question: In a Young’s Double Slit Experiment (YDSE), the central point $O$ on the screen lies on the perpendicular bisector of the two slits, so the geometric path difference at $O$ is zero and the central fringe is normally bright. You are asked to create a modification of the setup such that the central fringe at $O$ becomes dark. In your Answer, you must: (i) state the additional optical path difference required at $O$ to make it a dark fringe, and (ii) design a practical modification using a thin transparent sheet of refractive index $n$ placed in front of one slit, and derive the required thickness $t$ in terms of $\lambda$ and $n$.

options.A: Insert a thin transparent sheet of refractive index $n$ and thickness $t=\dfrac{\lambda}{2(n-1)}$ in front of one slit so that an additional path difference $\dfrac{\lambda}{2}$ is introduced at $O$.
options.B: Immerse the entire YDSE setup in a liquid; this automatically makes the central fringe dark because the wavelength changes in the liquid.
options.C: Use a source emitting two wavelengths simultaneously; the overlap of patterns guarantees the central fringe becomes dark.
options.D: Insert a thin transparent sheet of refractive index $n$ and thickness $t=\dfrac{\lambda}{(n-1)}$ in front of one slit so that an additional path difference $\lambda$ is introduced at $O$.
